verses.1: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying:
verses.2: Take a scroll and write on it all the words that I have spoken to you about Israel, Judah, and all the nations, from the day I began speaking to you during the days of Josiah until now.
verses.3: Perhaps the house of Judah will hear all the evil that I have planned to do to them, so that they may turn from their evil ways and I may forgive their iniquity and their sin.
verses.4: So Jeremiah called Baruch the son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the LORD that the prophet had spoken to him.
verses.5: And Jeremiah gave instructions to Baruch, saying, "I am being watched, so I cannot go into the house of the LORD.
verses.6: But you, go and read in the scroll all the words that I have spoken to you in the ears of the people in the house of the LORD on a day of fasting, and in the ears of all Judah who come from their cities."
verses.7: Perhaps their plea will come before the LORD, and they will turn from their evil ways, for the anger and wrath are great that the LORD has spoken against this people."
verses.8: Baruch did everything that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him to do, reading the words of the LORD in the house of the LORD.
verses.9: Now in the fifth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, a fast was proclaimed before the LORD for all the people in Jerusalem and for all the people coming from the cities of Judah to Jerusalem.
verses.10: Baruch read the words of Jeremiah in the house of the LORD in the chamber of Gemaryahu the son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court, at the entrance of the new gate, in the ears of all the people.
verses.11: And Michaiah the son of Gemaryahu the son of Shaphan heard all the words of the LORD from the scroll.
verses.12: So he went down to the palace of the king, to the chamber of the scribe, where the officials were sitting: Elashem the scribe, Delaiyahu the son of Shemaiah, and Elnatan the son of Acbor, Gemaryahu the son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah the son of Hananiah, and all the officials.
verses.13: And Michaiah told them all the words that Baruch had read in the ears of the people.
verses.14: So all the officials sent Jehudi the son of Nethaniah the son of Shalmayahu the son of Cushiy to Baruch, saying, "Bring the scroll in your hand, and come to us." And Baruch took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
verses.15: Then they said to him, "Please sit down and read it to us in our ears." And Baruch read it to them.
verses.16: And when they had heard all the words, they were afraid of each other and said to Baruch, "We must tell the king all these words."
verses.17: Then they asked Baruch, "Tell us, how did you write all these words from his mouth?"
verses.18: And Baruch said to them, "He read to me all these words, and I wrote them down with ink in the scroll."
verses.19: Then the officials said to Baruch, "Go and hide, you and Jeremiah, and let no man know where you are."
verses.20: So they went into the court of the king and left the scroll in the chamber of Elashem the scribe, and they told the king all these words in his ears.
verses.21: The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and Jehudi took it from the chamber of Elashem the scribe, and read it in the ears of the king and in the ears of all the officials standing over the king.
verses.22: Now the king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month, and a firepot was placed before him.
verses.23: So when Jehudi had read three or four columns, he cut them off with the scribe's knife and cast them into the firepot, until the entire scroll was burned in the fire.
verses.24: The king and all his attendants who heard all these words did not show fear or tear their clothes.
verses.25: Also, El Nathan and Delaiyahu and Gemaryahu tried to stop the king from burning the scroll, but the king would not listen to them.
verses.26: Then the king gave orders to Jerahmeel the son of the king, and to Seraiah the son of Azariah, and to Shelemiah the son of Abdeel, to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. And the LORD hid them.
verses.27: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah after the king had burned the scroll, and the words that Baruch had written from the mouth of Jeremiah, saying:
verses.28: Take another scroll and write on it all the words that were on the first scroll, which the king of Judah burned.
verses.29: And concerning the king of Judah, you will say: Thus says the LORD: You have burned this scroll, asking, "Why did you write on it, saying, 'The king of Babylon will certainly come and destroy this land, and will remove man and beast from it'?"
verses.30: Therefore thus says the LORD about Jehoiakim the king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on the throne of David, and his corpse will be cast out in the day and in the night.
verses.31: And I will bring upon him and upon his descendants and upon his servants the guilt of their iniquity, and I will bring upon them, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the people of Judah, all the evil that I have spoken to them, and they did not listen.
verses.32: So Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch the son of Neriah the scribe, and he wrote on it from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the scroll that Jehoiakim the king of Judah had burned, and many more words were added to them like these.

notes:
Notes
- v. 23: The Hebrew text uses "three and four" to denote the number of columns or sections of the scroll burned. The exact count is not specified, but the phrase is rendered as "three or four columns."
- v. 31: "I will bring upon them" reflects the nuance of the Hebrew verb פקד (to bring or cause to come), which can imply divine judgment or accountability.
- v. 32: The phrase "many more words were added to them like these" reflects the Hebrew, which uses a comparative structure to emphasize that the new scroll contained additional content beyond what was previously written.
